key_insight: The Universal Classifier reframes node, edge, and graph prediction as one similarity-based classification problem, enabling a single graph model to handle arbitrary feature and label dimensions.
engineering_relevance: For graph-heavy engineering workflows, this offers a path to reusable pretrained models that can transfer across heterogeneous datasets without redesigning the input schema for each task.
method: Lifts features and labels into 3D latent tensors to unify node-, edge-, and graph-level objectives.
Learns transferable representations by maximizing latent-space similarity instead of relying on fixed feature dimensions.
Supports zero-shot use on unseen graphs for classification, regression, and link prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong zero-shot transfer performance across node-, link-, and graph-level tasks on evaluations spanning those prediction settings.
watch_item: Practical deployment may still be limited by how well the learned latent similarity objective handles highly domain-specific graph semantics or noisy, incomplete features.
paper_title: The Universal Classifier for Graph Learning
